div.p: This project develops, tests, and uses digital methods to visualize the braided narrative, an understudied genre of the novel developed by prominent, diverse authors. Braided narratives differ from novels that focus on the same sequence of events from multiple points of view, a favourite form of detective or mystery novels since Wilkie Collins’s The Woman in White. Braided narratives also differ from short story collections where each unit works independently.

Authors can use the innovative formal structure of braided narratives to respond to the questions and challenges that characterize our era. For example, Nicole Krauss’s The History of Love (2005) alternates between three main narrators to trace the intergenerational trauma of the Holocaust, and Louise Erdrich’s The Plague of Doves (2008) moves between five narrators to test the potential for reconciliation.
